title: Economic Calendar API Guide
heading: Analysis — Economic calendar
intro: Scheduled economic releases, keyed by event and time, with the instruments each one moves. A background worker keeps the listing current and watches the minutes around a print so an actual lands as soon as it is published.
Reads never fetch — they serve what the worker last saved.

endpoints.title: Scheduled releases
endpoints.desc: Events in a window, filtered by instrument, currency or impact. Symbols are forgiving: gold, xauusd and XAU/USD all resolve.

params.name: symbol
params.desc: Only events that move this instrument — both currency legs for an FX pair.

params.name: impact
params.desc: high | moderate | low, comma-separated. Most real market movers are tagged moderate.

params.name: range
params.desc: Named preset (today, yesterday, this_week) or last-<N>-<unit> — last-30-minutes, last-6-hours, last-3-days, last-2-weeks, last-6-months, last-1-years. Months and years are 30 and 365 days; use since/until when the boundary must be exact.

params.name: hours
params.desc: The next N hours instead of a named range.

params.name: pretend_date
params.desc: Answer as if the request were made on this UTC date — e.g. ?pretend_date=2026-08-25&pretend_time=13:12. For backtests and agent reruns that must not see the outcome. Left off, you get the present.

params.name: pretend_time
params.desc: UTC time of day to pair with pretend_date, e.g. 13:12. Omitted, the moment is midnight — not the whole day.

examples.label: By range — the last 6 hours
examples.hint: last-<N>-<unit> works on every data API: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months or years.

endpoints.title: Worker health
endpoints.desc: Is the calendar still arriving? Last fetch, how many events are held, and the last failure if there was one.

notes: Filtering to high impact alone throws away most of a day's events — Employment Cost Index, Chicago PMI and Michigan Sentiment are all tagged moderate. high,moderate is usually what you want.

Any read here accepts pretend_date and pretend_time (UTC) and answers as of that moment: ?pretend_date=2026-08-25&pretend_time=13:12. Anything published later is hidden. Anything merely SCHEDULED for later survives with its actual blanked and pretend_pending set — the schedule was known in advance, the number was not. Responses carry X-Pretend-Time so a replay is never mistaken for the present.
